terminal.description: A shell that starts in the shop's top folder. Build each chain one command at a time and read what it prints.

tasks.title: List what sold at the market
tasks.description:
`market/sold.txt` has one line per sale, so most items appear many times. Save every item that was sold, each one only once, in alphabetical order, into `items.txt` in the top folder.

Check compares `items.txt` with the items in `market/sold.txt`: each once, nothing else, in alphabetical order.
nextSteps: Look at the start of `market/sold.txt` with `head`.
Sort its lines and read the result: equal items now sit together.
Pipe that into the command that drops repeats.
Save the end of the chain with `>`.
hints: Two commands from the lesson, joined with a pipe, do this.
`uniq` only drops a line that repeats the one right above it, so `sort` has to come first.
Run `sort market/sold.txt | uniq > items.txt` from the top folder.

tasks.title: Find the five best sellers
tasks.description:
Hesper wants the five items that sold most at the market, each with how many were sold, the best seller first. Save those five lines, a count and an item on each, into `top-five.txt` in the top folder.

Check reads the count and the item on each line of `top-five.txt` and compares them with `market/sold.txt`: the right counts, the five biggest, the biggest first.
nextSteps: Start from the chain of the last task, and make it count each item.
Sort that by the numbers, the biggest first, and read it.
Keep only the first five lines.
Save it with `>` and look at it with `cat`.
hints: The lesson's part on `uniq` shows an option that counts, and the part on `sort` shows how to sort by number.
`uniq -c` counts equal lines that sit together, `sort -rn` puts the biggest number first, and `head -n` keeps the top lines. Join them with pipes.
Run `sort market/sold.txt | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -n 5 > top-five.txt` from the top folder.

tasks.title: Add today's finished jobs to the list
tasks.description:
`jobs-done.txt` is Idris's running list of every finished job. Add the lines of `logs/today.log` that end in `finished` to the end of it, each once, and keep every line it already holds, in its order.

Check compares `jobs-done.txt` with the lines it started with, followed by today's finished jobs.
nextSteps: Search the log for the finished jobs and read what that prints.
Add that output to the end of `jobs-done.txt`, without replacing what is there.
Look at the end of `jobs-done.txt` with `tail`.
hints: `>` would replace the whole list. The lesson shows a way to add to the end of a file.
`grep` finds the finished lines, and `>>` adds what a command prints to the end of a file. Run it once only.
Run `grep finished logs/today.log >> jobs-done.txt` from the top folder.

tasks.title: Sort the stock list in place
tasks.description:
Put `stock.txt` itself in alphabetical order, with every line it holds now. The sorted list must end up in `stock.txt`, not only in another file.

Check reads `stock.txt` and compares it with its lines at the start, in alphabetical order.
nextSteps: Print it sorted, without saving anything, and read it.
Save the sorted lines under a new name, and look at that file.
Move the new file over `stock.txt`, and look at `stock.txt` again.
hints: Saving into the file a command reads empties it first. The lesson's part on when `>` destroys shows a safe way.
Sort into a new file, check it, then use `mv` to put it where `stock.txt` is.
Run `sort stock.txt > stock-sorted.txt`, then `mv stock-sorted.txt stock.txt`.
